title: Adult Coconut Palm Soil Health, Basin Nutrition & Irrigation Advisory
text: Coconut (Cocos nucifera) adult bearing palm management requires balanced macro and micronutrient supplementation for optimal nut yield. For adult palms aged 8 years and above, apply 1.3 kg Urea (560g N), 2.0 kg Single Superphosphate (320g P2O5), and 2.0 kg Muriate of Potash (1200g K2O) per palm per year in two equal splits: the first split during May-June (pre-monsoon) and the second split during September-October (post-monsoon). Supplement with 50 kg of well-decomposed Farm Yard Manure (FYM) or green manure per palm annually. In drought-prone coastal tracts of Tamil Nadu (such as Thoothukudi), drip irrigation at 60 to 80 litres per palm per day is mandatory. Basin mulching with coconut coir pith or dried coconut fronds conserves 35-40% soil moisture. Inspect leaf axils monthly for Rhinoceros Beetle (Oryctes rhinoceros); hook out adult beetles with an iron spear and fill top leaf axils with a 1:1 mixture of neem cake and river sand. For Red Palm Weevil (Rhynchophorus ferrugineus), avoid making injuries on trunk and swab wounds with coal tar.
fertilizer_schedule: Apply 1.3 kg Urea, 2.0 kg Superphosphate, and 2.0 kg MOP per palm per year in two splits (May-June & Sept-Oct). Add 50 kg Farm Yard Manure (FYM) and 500g Borax.
water_management: Drip irrigation @ 60-80 litres of water per palm per day. Basin mulching with coconut coir pith or dried fronds to maintain root moisture.
pest_management: Monitor for Rhinoceros Beetle (hook out beetles, fill leaf axils with neem cake + sand) and Red Palm Weevil. Place pheromone traps for surveillance.
citation_source: ICAR-CPCRI Technical Bulletin No. 98: Coconut Palm Management, pp. 18-24.
publisher: ICAR - Central Plantation Crops Research Institute

title: Young Coconut Seedling Establishment & Vegetative Nutrition Advisory
text: During the initial vegetative establishment phase (1 to 4 years post planting), coconut seedlings require gentle, progressive nutrient splits to build sturdy bole and root architecture. Apply one-fourth of the adult dose in the first year (140g N, 80g P2O5, 300g K2O), one-half in the second year, three-fourths in the third year, and full adult dose from the fourth year onwards. Apply 15-20 litres of water per seedling every other day during dry summer months. Protect from sunscald by shading with coconut leaves during first two summers. Mulch basins with green manure (Crotalaria juncea) sown and incorporated in situ. Prevent termites by applying Chlorpyrifos 20 EC @ 2.5 ml/L in basin if infesting sandy loam soils.
fertilizer_schedule: Quarter dose: 325g Urea, 500g SSP, 500g MOP per seedling per year along with 15 kg compost in two splits (June and October).
water_management: Irrigate with 15-20 litres water per seedling every alternate day. Mulch 1m basin around seedling collar.
pest_management: Monitor for black headed caterpillar and termite damage. Spray Chlorpyrifos 20 EC around seedling basin if termite tunnels appear.
citation_source: ICAR-CPCRI Technical Bulletin No. 98: Coconut Palm Management, pp. 10-14.
publisher: ICAR - Central Plantation Crops Research Institute

title: Paddy Vegetative Stage Nutrition, Tillering & AWD Water Advisory
text: During the active tillering vegetative stage of transplanted lowland rice (Oryza sativa), adequate nitrogen and zinc nutrition are critical to maximize productive panicle count per square meter. Apply Nitrogen @ 25 kg/ha as first top dressing at active tillering (15-20 days after transplanting). Apply Zinc Sulfate @ 25 kg/ha as soil application or spray 0.5% ZnSO4 on foliage if deficiency symptoms (khaira / leaf bronzing) appear. Maintain shallow submergence of 2-3 cm during initial establishment, then practice Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) using field water tubes to save 25-30% irrigation water while promoting deep root aeration. Monitor for Yellow Stem Borer (Scirpophaga incertulas) dead hearts and Leaf Folder (Cnaphalocrocis medinalis). If ETL is reached (10% dead hearts or 2 folded leaves/hill), spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3 ml/L or Flubendiamide 39.35% SC @ 0.2 ml/L.
fertilizer_schedule: Apply Nitrogen @ 25 kg/ha as top dressing along with Zinc Sulfate (25 kg/ha). Maintain 50:25:25 NPK basal ratio.
water_management: Maintain shallow submergence of 2-3 cm. Practice Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) to enhance root aeration.
pest_management: Monitor for Stem Borer and Leaf Folder. Spray Neem oil @ 3% or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3 ml/L if ETL crossed.
citation_source: TNAU Crop Production Guide (Agriculture) 2024, Section 1.2: Rice Agronomy, pp. 48-52.

title: Paddy Panicle Initiation & Flowering Stage Reproductive Advisory
text: At panicle initiation and 50% flowering stage, water stress or nutrient imbalance directly reduces spikelet fertility and grain filling percentage. Top dress final Nitrogen split @ 25 kg/ha along with Muriate of Potash (MOP) @ 15 kg/ha at panicle initiation (PI stage) to ensure full panicle emergence and robust starch accumulation. Ensure continuous shallow standing water of 5 cm throughout the flowering and milk stages; drought stress at anthesis results in catastrophic sterile spikelets. Scout field borders for False Smut (Ustilaginoidea virens) and Brown Plant Hopper (BPH - Nilaparvata lugens). Drain water completely for 2-3 days if BPH population exceeds 1 hopper per tiller to break microclimate humidity. Spray Pymetrozine 50 WG @ 0.6 g/L if BPH exceeds ETL.
fertilizer_schedule: Apply final split of Muriate of Potash (MOP) @ 15 kg/ha and Nitrogen @ 25 kg/ha to ensure proper grain filling.
water_management: Ensure standing water of 5 cm throughout flowering; avoid moisture stress to prevent chaffy grains.
pest_management: Scout for False Smut and Brown Plant Hopper (BPH). Avoid excess nitrogen application. Spray Pymetrozine 50 WG if ETL exceeded.
citation_source: TNAU Crop Production Guide (Agriculture) 2024, Section 1.4: Rice Reproductive Management, pp. 54-56.

title: Banana Bunch Development & Pseudostem Nutrition Advisory
text: Banana (Musa acuminata) during shooting and bunch development (7th to 10th month) demands high potash nutrition for bunch length, hand compactness, and finger grade. Apply 50g Urea and 100g MOP per plant at 7th and 8th month in soil basin followed by light irrigation. Spray Potassium Dihydrogen Phosphate (0.5%) + Urea (1%) twice at 15-day intervals after complete bunch emergence. Provide propping with bamboo poles or casuarina poles to prevent wind lodging under coastal sea breezes. Remove male bud (denavelling) immediately after last hand emerges to hasten bunch maturity by 10-12 days. Sleeve bunch with 100-gauge perforated white polyethylene sleeves to guard against thrips and sunburn. Swab pseudostem with Carbaryl 50 WP (2g/L) to prevent Banana Pseudostem Weevil (Odoiporus longicollis) larval tunneling.
fertilizer_schedule: Apply 50g Urea and 100g MOP per plant at 7th and 8th month. Spray Micronutrient mixture @ 0.5% on leaves after bunch emergence.
water_management: Irrigate daily through drip system @ 15-20 litres per plant. Avoid water stagnation to prevent Fusarium wilt.
pest_management: Inspect pseudostem for Banana Borer. Inject monocrotophos/chlorpyrifos or swab stem base with carbaryl. Sleeve bunches.
citation_source: National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB) Field Manual 2024, pp. 12-16.
publisher: ICAR - National Research Centre for Banana

title: Banana Early Vegetative Sucker & Canopy Management Advisory
text: From sucker establishment to 5th month vegetative growth, focus is on expanding broad photosynthetic leaf area. Apply 100g Urea, 150g SSP, and 100g MOP in 3 splits at 2nd, 3rd, and 4th month post planting. Inoculate roots with Vesicular Arbuscular Mycorrhiza (VAM) @ 250g/plant and Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 50g/plant at planting. Perform regular desuckering, retaining only mother plant until bunch initiation. Monitor for Banana Aphid (Pentalonia nigronervosa), the vector for Banana Bunchy Top Virus (BBTV); spray Dimethoate 30 EC @ 1.5 ml/L if colonies appear in leaf axils.
fertilizer_schedule: Apply 100g Urea, 150g SSP, and 100g MOP per plant in 3 split applications at 2nd, 3rd, and 4th month.
water_management: Drip irrigation @ 10-12 litres per plant per day. Maintain clean weed-free root zone basin.
pest_management: Inspect leaf axils for Pentalonia aphid vectors. Destroy BBTV infected plants immediately.
citation_source: National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB) Field Manual 2024, pp. 6-9.
publisher: ICAR - National Research Centre for Banana

title: Maize Vegetative Growth & Fall Armyworm (FAW) Protocol
text: Maize (Zea mays) vegetative growth requires prompt nitrogen top-dressing at knee-high stage (30-35 days after sowing). Apply Urea @ 55 kg/ha as top dressing along the furrow after inter-cultivation and earthing up. Pre-irrigate before fertilizer application to ensure rapid root uptake. CRITICAL PEST ALERT: Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) infests maize whorls during 15-45 DAS. Scout 20 consecutive plants in 5 field spots. If windowing or fresh frass is seen in >5% whorls, apply sand + neem cake mixture (9:1) into whorls, or spray Spinetoram 11.7 SC @ 0.5 ml/L or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC @ 0.4 ml/L using high-volume knapsack sprayer directed into leaf whorls.
fertilizer_schedule: Top dress Urea @ 55 kg/ha at knee-high stage (30 DAS). Ensure soil moisture prior to fertilizer application.
water_management: Irrigate at critical vegetative growth stages (every 8-10 days depending on soil type).
pest_management: CRITICAL: Scout weekly for Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda). Apply Metarhizium anisopliae or Spinetoram 11.7 SC @ 0.5 ml/L.
citation_source: ICAR-IIMR Maize Agronomy Advisory & TNAU Guidelines, pp. 31-35.
publisher: ICAR - Indian Institute of Millets Research

title: Cotton Squaring & Peak Flowering Canopy Nutrition Advisory
text: In black cotton and red loamy soils of southern Tamil Nadu, peak flowering (60-80 DAS) requires balanced potassium and boron to prevent shedding of squares and young bolls. Apply Urea @ 45 kg/ha and MOP @ 35 kg/ha as second top-dressing. Foliar spray 1% Magnesium Sulfate (MgSO4) + 1% Urea at 60 and 75 DAS to prevent red leaf disease. Spray Borax @ 0.2% (2g/L) during peak flowering to enhance boll set. Monitor for American Bollworm (Helicoverpa armigera) and Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella). Install delta sticky traps with Gossyplure @ 5 traps/ha. Spray Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG @ 0.5 g/L if rosetted flowers exceed 5%.
fertilizer_schedule: Top dress Urea @ 45 kg/ha and MOP @ 35 kg/ha. Foliar spray 1% MgSO4 + 1% Urea to prevent leaf reddening.
water_management: Irrigate at 12-15 day intervals in furrows. Avoid water stress during square initiation and flowering.
pest_management: Install pheromone traps for Pink Bollworm. Spray Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG if rosetted flower incidence exceeds 5%.
citation_source: ICAR-CICR Cotton Production Technologies & TNAU Guide 2024, pp. 62-68.
publisher: ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research

title: Groundnut Flowering, Pegging & Pod Calcium Enrichment Advisory
text: Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea) during flowering and peg penetration (35-50 DAS) has an essential demand for calcium in the pod formation zone (top 5 cm soil). Apply Gypsum @ 400 kg/ha at 40-45 DAS around plant base and incorporate by earthing up. Gypsum provides both calcium (for shell hardening and pod filling) and sulfur (for oil synthesis), preventing hollow heart and blind nuts (pops). Maintain soil moisture during pegging; dry soil prevents geotropic peg entry. Scout for Spodoptera litura and Rust (Puccinia arachidis). Spray Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2g/L if rust pustules appear on lower leaf surface.
fertilizer_schedule: Apply Gypsum @ 400 kg/ha at 40-45 DAS (flowering/pegging) by earthing up. Spray 0.5% Ferrous Sulfate + 0.1% Citric Acid if iron chlorosis occurs.
water_management: Ensure adequate soil moisture during flowering and peg penetration (irrigate every 10 days). Avoid waterlogging.
pest_management: Monitor for Leaf Miner and Rust. Spray Chlorothalonil 75 WP @ 2g/L or Hexaconazole 5 EC @ 1 ml/L if leaf rust appears.
citation_source: ICAR-DGR Groundnut Production Manual & TNAU Guidelines 2024, pp. 22-27.

title: Sugarcane Grand Growth Phase Elongation & Stem Borer Advisory
text: During grand growth and stalk elongation (120 to 240 days), sugarcane demands high moisture and final nitrogen-potash split. Apply final top-dressing of Urea @ 60 kg/ha and MOP @ 40 kg/ha at 120-150 days followed by thorough earthing up to create deep ridges and furrows. Trash mulching @ 5 t/ha in furrows saves up to 30% irrigation water and suppresses weeds. Irrigate every 7-10 days depending on climate. Detrash lower dry senescent leaves at 5th and 7th month to improve field aeration and deter scale insects. Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis @ 2.5 cc/ha for biological control of internode borer (Chilo sacchariphagus indicus).
fertilizer_schedule: Final split: Urea @ 60 kg/ha and MOP @ 40 kg/ha at 150 days followed by earthing up.
water_management: Trash mulching in furrows. Irrigate every 7-10 days during elongation phase.
pest_management: Release Trichogramma chilonis egg parasitoids against Internode borer. Detrash dry leaves at 5th and 7th month.
citation_source: TNAU Crop Production Guide (Agriculture) 2024: Sugarcane Chapter, pp. 88-94.
